covered: Magma versus lava; the three ways magma is generated (decompression, added heat, added water); the Benioff-zone payoff promised at the end of Lesson 7 — slab dewatering lowers the melting point of the mantle wedge and generates arc magma.
Viscosity (silica content and temperature) and gas content as the two dials controlling effusive versus explosive eruption; the shaken-fizzy-bottle analogy.
Shield, composite and cinder-cone volcanoes derived from magma chemistry; the three-profile comparison figure.

Crater versus caldera; caldera examples (Yellowstone ~640 ka, Krakatoa 1883, Toba ~74 ka); fissure eruptions and flood basalt provinces; the origin of the word 'traps'; the mid-ocean ridge as the largest volcanic system.
The Ring of Fire (Pacific rim, ~40,000 km, majority of active volcanoes and earthquakes) and the mid-ocean ridge and Mediterranean belts.

Subduction-zone versus hotspot volcanism — setting, magma source and temperament; the 100–150 km depth rule for arcs; Hawaii's age-progressive chain and the Emperor seamount bend; Yellowstone as a continental hotspot.

Hazards: pyroclastic flows (Mount Pelée 1902), lahars (Nevado del Ruiz 1985), ash fall, sulphate aerosols and the 1816 'year without a summer' after Tambora 1815. Benefits: fertile volcanic soils, geothermal energy, minerals and building stone, outgassing and the early atmosphere.

India's volcanic legacy: the Deccan Traps (fissure-fed flood basalt, ~66 Ma, ~5 lakh km², up to ~2 km thick near the Western Ghats, K–Pg debate, Réunion plume link), regur/black cotton soil, Ajanta–Ellora carved in basalt, and Barren Island as India's only active volcano on the Andaman arc in seismic Zone V, with Narcondam dormant.
lastHandoff.next: Mountain Building and the Rock Cycle — Orogeny and mountain types (fold, fault-block, volcanic, residual); fold structures (anticline, syncline, nappe); faulting and rift valleys; the Himalayas as a collision mountain; isostasy and mountain roots; the rock cycle linking igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks; why the rock cycle is a system.
lastHandoff.notes: The 'india-seismic-zones' figure was reused verbally for Barren Island (Andaman arc = Zone V) as planned; keep reusing it for any disaster-management or hazard-mapping question. The new 'volcano-profiles' figure is the master volcano figure — it can be reused for any question on volcano types or magma chemistry, and pairs naturally with 'plate-boundaries' from Lesson 6. The new 'subduction-vs-hotspot' cross-section is the figure to reuse whenever the exam asks to distinguish tectonic settings, and it also revives the Benioff zone visually. The new 'ring-of-fire' map deliberately extends the 'map as argument' stance from Lesson 1 and marks the Deccan Traps, so it can be reused in an Indian-geography or resource-geography context.
